title: Wijnreis door de Bourgogne: wijnbars in Beaune en wijnhuizen in de Côte d'Or
description: Waar je in Beaune een glas Bourgogne drinkt, welke wijnhuizen je kunt bezoeken en waar je eet: zo plan je een wijnreis door de Bourgogne.
title_en: A wine trip through Burgundy: wine bars in Beaune and wineries in the Côte d'Or
description_en: Where to drink a glass of Burgundy in Beaune, which wineries you can visit and where to eat: how to plan a wine trip through Burgundy.
body_en:
Beaune is the best base for a wine trip through Burgundy. The centre has dozens of wine bars, and within half an hour's drive you are in the famous wine villages of the Côte d'Or. Below, where to drink a glass in Beaune, which wineries you can visit and where to eat in the villages.

## The region in brief

The Côte d'Or is a narrow strip of hills some fifty kilometres long. In the north is the **Côte de Nuits**, with villages such as Gevrey-Chambertin and Vosne-Romanée and mostly red wine from Pinot Noir. In the south is the **Côte de Beaune**, home also to the great white wines from Chardonnay, from Meursault, Puligny- and Chassagne-Montrachet. Chablis is separate, more than an hour's drive north, with taut Chardonnay on limestone.

## Wine bars in Beaune

[L'Arche des Vins](/en/locations/larche-des-vins) is in a medieval street and is a wine bar and wine shop in one, with French dishes and a terrace. [La Dilettante](/en/locations/la-dilettante) on the Rue du Faubourg Bretonnière is open for lunch, dinner and a late glass, with small dishes. On the edge of the centre, [Le Bout du Monde](/en/locations/la-bout-du-monde) has a big cellar with plenty of Burgundy and a terrace for after a long day of tasting. [Le Comptoir des Tontons](/en/locations/le-comptoir-des-tontons), with the red façade, is bistro, wine bar and wine shop at once.

On the Place Ziem is [Bistrot du Coin](/en/locations/bistrot-du-coin), a small wine café where the owner is happy to help you plan which estates to visit. [La Maison du Colombier](/en/locations/la-maison-du-colombier) is a gastro bar with plenty of wine and tapas, where you can also stay the night. If after a day of Burgundy you want something different, [Enstase](/en/locations/enstase) has bao and tapas. At [Loiseau des Vignes](/en/locations/loiseau-des-vignes), close to the Hospices, you can choose from 32 wines by the glass from four climate-controlled cabinets.

![L'Arche des Vins in Beaune](/uploads/larche-des-vins.webp)

## Tasting in Beaune

At [Maison Denis Perret](/en/locations/maison-denis-perret) on the Place Carnot you can taste the wines of five large négociants, including Bouchard, Drouhin and Jadot. Under the cobblestones of Beaune lie the cellars of [Patriarche](/en/locations/patriarche-père-et-fils), five kilometres of tunnels with more than two million bottles. You walk around on your own with an audio guide. Smaller is [Coudurier Jung](/en/locations/vins-coudurier-jung), an urban winery with a cellar of a handful of barrels, without filtration and with little sulphur. [Domaine des Croix](/en/locations/domaine-des-croix) receives visitors by appointment, except in September and October.

## The Côte de Beaune

In Meursault, the [Caveau de l'Hôtel Les Charmes](/en/locations/caveau-de-lhotel-les-charmes) pours almost 500 wines, including all the premiers crus of Meursault, at shop price plus €10. Just down the road you eat at [Le Soufflot](/en/locations/le-soufflot), in an old winegrower's house. In a side street of Chassagne-Montrachet is [Colette](/en/locations/colette), a wine bar with a cellar where you can also buy bottles at good prices.

In Savigny-lès-Beaune, [Chandon de Briailles](/en/locations/chandon-de-briailles) has farmed biodynamically since 2005, with vineyards in three villages. [Domaine Rapet](/en/locations/domaine-rapet-père-fils) in Pernand-Vergelesses, at the foot of the Corton, has made wine for more than 250 years. In Auxey-Duresses, monks from Cluny planted the vineyards of [Le Clos du Moulin aux Moines](/en/locations/le-clos-du-moulin-aux-moines) in 962, with a windmill above the vines. And at [Réserve de Bacchus](/en/locations/reserve-de-bacchus) in Ladoix-Serrigny there are more than 1,000 wines, handy for taking a few bottles home at the end of your trip.

## The Côte de Nuits and Chablis

In Vosne-Romanée, Louis-Michel Liger-Belair opened [La Cuverie](/en/locations/la-cuverie-de-vosne) in 2022, a meeting place looking out on the Clos du Château. [Domaine Trapet](/en/locations/domaine-trapet) in Gevrey-Chambertin receives a maximum of four people at a time, with a Burgundian meal and five wines.

In Chablis, [Chablis Wine Not](/en/locations/chablis-wine-not) is in an old pharmacy, and the winemakers drink there themselves. [Domaine Duplessis](/en/locations/domaine-duplessis) has premiers crus and grand cru Les Clos, from vines that are 75 years or older on many plots.

## Tip

At most small estates in Burgundy you need an appointment, and during the harvest in September and October many houses take no visitors. In the wine bars of Beaune and Meursault you taste the wines of estates you can't visit. All addresses are also in the [Burgundy guide](/en/wine-travel/burgundy).

title: Cava proeven in de Penedès: wijnhuizen bij Barcelona
description: Van kelders van zes verdiepingen in Sant Sadurní tot biodynamische wijnhuizen: zo bezoek je de mousserende wijnen van de Penedès, op een uur van Barcelona.
title_en: Tasting cava in the Penedès: wineries near Barcelona
description_en: From six-storey cellars in Sant Sadurní to biodynamic estates: how to visit the sparkling wines of the Penedès, an hour from Barcelona.
body_en:
An hour's drive from Barcelona lies the Penedès, where most Spanish sparkling wine comes from. Cava is made like Champagne, with a second fermentation in the bottle, but from different grapes: mainly Xarel·lo, Macabeo and Parellada. Many of the best houses work organically or biodynamically, and some have left the DO Cava to follow stricter rules of their own. Below are the wineries you can visit.

## Sant Sadurní d'Anoia

Sant Sadurní is the capital of cava, and many houses have their cellars right in the town. Under [Recaredo](/en/locations/recaredo) is the cellar Josep Mata Capellades began building under his house in 1924. All the wines are brut nature, without added sugar, from a single vintage and disgorged by hand. At [Juvé & Camps](/en/locations/juvé-camps) you walk through six floors of tunnels, where the bottles are still turned by hand.

[Jaume Giró i Giró](/en/locations/jaume-giró-i-giró), with its yellow façade, and [Cava Blancher](/en/locations/blancher-capdevila-pujol) on the Plaça del Pont Romà are also right in the centre, with cellars on several floors underground. Just outside the town, [Celler Kripta](/en/locations/celler-kripta) makes Kripta, a sparkling wine in an amphora-shaped bottle that ages for around eight years.

![The cellars of Recaredo in Sant Sadurní](/uploads/recaredo.webp)

## Gelida and Subirats

[Torelló](/en/locations/torelló-viticultors) in Gelida has documents going back to 1395 and 23 generations of winegrowing, with 135 hectares of organic vineyards around two medieval masias. In Subirats, [Sumarroca](/en/locations/sumarroca) has organic vineyards on a large estate between Sant Sadurní and Monistrol d'Anoia. In Sant Pau d'Ordal, [Albet i Noya](/en/locations/albet-i-noya) became Spain's first organic winemaker. After tasting, eat in the same village at [Cal Xim](/en/locations/cal-xim), where they have grilled lamb chops over oak for more than fifty years.

## The rest of the Penedès

[Parés Baltà](/en/locations/parés-baltà) in Pacs del Penedès has made wine since 1790. The estate is biodynamic, and its own sheep graze the land. [Can Ràfols dels Caus](/en/locations/can-ràfols-dels-caus) in the Garraf massif pioneered fermenting Xarel·lo in chestnut barrels. [Caves Bolet](/en/locations/caves-bolet) in Castellví de la Marca has been organic since 2003, and you can stay in a modernist house from 1911. [Heretat Baltà de Cela](/en/locations/heretat-baltà-de-cela) in Guardiola de Font-rubí makes a sparkling wine from Xarel·lo alone that ages for five years. [Jean Leon](/en/locations/jean-leon) in Torrelavit was the first winery in Spain to make a wine from Cabernet Sauvignon alone.

## Around Barcelona

In Alella, fifteen kilometres north of Barcelona, [Alella Vinícola](/en/locations/alella-vinícola) is in a modernist building by a pupil of Gaudí. If you want to head further inland, go to [Abadal](/en/locations/abadal) in the Bages, where the white Picapoll grows.

## Tip

Most wineries only receive visitors by appointment. By train from Barcelona you are in Sant Sadurní in an hour, where you can visit several cellars on foot. All addresses are also in the [Barcelona & Penedès guide](/en/wine-travel/barcelona-penedes).

title: Champagne bezoeken: kleine wijnhuizen en champagnebars in Reims en Épernay
description: Kleine champagnehuizen, champagnebars met honderden growers en waar je eet: zo plan je een wijnreis door de Champagne.
title_en: Visiting Champagne: small growers and Champagne bars in Reims and Épernay
description_en: Small Champagne houses, Champagne bars with hundreds of growers and where to eat: how to plan a wine trip through Champagne.
body_en:
Champagne is around four hours' drive from Utrecht, with Reims and Épernay at its centre. You can visit the big houses on the Avenue de Champagne, but the most fun are the small winemakers who grow their own grapes: the growers, or vignerons. You taste their Champagne in the wine bars of Reims and Épernay, or at the winemaker's home.

## The region in brief

There are three main areas. On the **Montagne de Reims**, between Reims and Épernay, mostly Pinot Noir grows, giving Champagne with body. In the **Côte des Blancs**, south of Épernay, it is almost all Chardonnay, for taut, fresh Blanc de Blancs. In the **Vallée de la Marne**, west of Épernay, there is a lot of Meunier, which gives fruity Champagne. Of the more than 300 wine villages, only 17 have grand cru status, such as Aÿ, Ambonnay, Cramant, Avize and Chouilly.

## Épernay

On the Avenue de Champagne, between the big houses, [#Brut](/en/locations/brut) pours only grower Champagne. A few minutes' walk away is [L'Atypique](/en/locations/latypique), a Champagne bar in an inner garden, with live music. At [Le 520](/en/locations/520) you can choose from 650 cuvées from more than 180 houses and vignerons. Every Saturday morning there is a free tasting with a winemaker.

To eat, book early at [La Cave à Champagne](/en/locations/la-cave-a-champagne), a family bistro with plenty of grower Champagne on the list. Ask for a table in the main room. [L'Oben](/en/locations/loben) is small, with room for 26 guests, and is often full of locals. [Sacré Bistro](/en/locations/sacré-bistro) pairs burgers with Champagne, as a stop between two cellar visits.

![#Brut on the Avenue de Champagne](/uploads/brutepernay.webp)

## Reims

In Reims the Champagne bars are close together in the centre. [Le Coq Rouge](/en/locations/le-coq-rouge) is small and always busy, with wines and Champagnes the team picks from the makers themselves. [Le Wine Bar by Le Vintage](/en/locations/le-wine-bar-by-le-vintage) on the Place du Forum has more than 500 wines and 200 Champagnes. Next door, Aude Henon opened [La Vertu](/en/locations/la-vertu) in 2025, with only Champagne and wine from small producers. [Le Clos](/en/locations/le-clos) is tucked away in an inner garden by the market hall, with a large terrace in summer.

At the foot of the cathedral, [Cave du 13OR](/en/locations/cave-du-13or) has a Champagne bar and a shop with 200 Champagnes. At [Les Caves du Forum](/en/locations/les-caves-du-forum) you walk down a stone staircase to three 16th-century cellars, nine metres underground.

## Visiting the growers

In the Côte des Blancs, [Diebolt-Vallois](/en/locations/diebolt-vallois) in Cramant makes Blanc de Blancs from vines planted in 1950. In Chouilly, [Cyrill Banchet](/en/locations/cyrill-banchet) makes Chardonnay on grand cru chalk. In Avize, at [Le Recommandé](/en/locations/le-recommandé), you can choose from more than 400 Champagnes from small growers of the Côte des Blancs, in the village where they are made.

On the Montagne de Reims, [Gatinois](/en/locations/gatinois) in Aÿ makes only grand cru, 90% Pinot Noir, around 50,000 bottles a year. [Egly-Ouriet](/en/locations/champagne-egly-ouriet) in Ambonnay ages its Champagne for three to four years, much longer than most makers. [Champagne Gardet](/en/locations/champagne-gardet) in Chigny-les-Roses is a small house with several tastings. [Roger Coulon](/en/locations/roger-coulon) in Vrigny works organically, without filtration, with the eighth and ninth generations.

In Hautvillers, the village of Dom Pérignon, [G. Tribaut](/en/locations/g-tribaut) welcomes visitors without complicated appointments. You eat there at [Le Beau Lieu](/en/locations/le-beau-lieu), where you pay the shop price for a bottle plus a small corkage fee. In the Vallée de la Marne are [Bochet-Lemoine](/en/locations/champagne-bochet-lemoine) in Cormoyeux and [Le Bateau Lavoir](/en/locations/le-bateau-lavoir) in Damery, on the Marne, a good lunch spot on a bike ride.

## Tip

At most small houses you need to book ahead. Plan no more than two or three a day, and in the wine bars of Reims and Épernay drink the Champagnes of makers you can't visit. All addresses are also in the [Champagne guide](/en/wine-travel/champagne).

title: Wijnreis langs de Moezel: riesling proeven van Trier tot Cochem
description: Van Trier via Bernkastel naar Cochem: welke wijnhuizen je langs de Moezel kunt bezoeken en waar je riesling drinkt.
title_en: A wine trip along the Mosel: tasting Riesling from Trier to Cochem
description_en: From Trier via Bernkastel to Cochem: which wineries you can visit along the Mosel and where to drink Riesling.
body_en:
The Mosel winds from Trier to Koblenz, with vineyards on slate slopes that are sometimes so steep everything has to be done by hand. Riesling grows almost everywhere, from bone-dry to sweet, with little alcohol and plenty of acidity. From the Netherlands it is four to five hours away. Below are the addresses, from upstream to downstream.

## Mosel Riesling

The best vineyards are on south-facing slopes along the river, where the water and the dark slate hold the warmth. The label often tells you how ripe the grapes were: Kabinett is light and fresh, Spätlese and Auslese riper and often a little sweeter. If you want a dry wine, look for the word **trocken**. The tributaries Saar and Ruwer are part of the region too. There the Riesling is often even tauter.

## Trier and the Ruwer

On the market square in Trier, looking out on the cathedral, [Kesselstatt](/en/locations/kesselstatt) has a Weinstube. You taste Riesling from famous vineyards of the Mosel, Saar and Ruwer side by side, such as Piesporter Goldtröpfchen and Bernkasteler Doctor. [Bagatelle](/en/locations/bagatelle) is right on the Mosel, with a terrace by the water and a list full of Riesling. Just outside Trier, on the Ruwer, lies [Maximin Grünhaus](/en/locations/maximin-grünhaus), where wine has been made for almost 2,000 years, first by the Romans and then by monks. Since 1882 the estate has belonged to the Von Schubert family.

## Bernkastel-Kues

Bernkastel is the prettiest wine town on the Mosel, with half-timbered houses and the Bernkasteler Doctor above the centre. [Dr. Loosen](/en/locations/weingut-dr-loosen) is on the World's 50 Best Vineyards list and has vineyards in the famous sites around Bernkastel. [Dr. Pauly-Bergweiler](/en/locations/weingut-dr-pauly-bergweiler) has fifteen plots between Brauneberg and Erden. Every Saturday at four there is a tasting with an explanation, in English too. To eat, go to [Graacher Tor](/en/locations/graacher-tor) in the medieval centre. The owner comes round the tables to help you with the wine.

![Weingut Dr. Loosen near Bernkastel](/uploads/weingut-dr-loosen.jpg)

## Traben-Trarbach and Cochem

In Traben-Trarbach, at [Die Mosel Vinothek](/en/locations/die-mosel-vinothek-winebar) on the promenade, you can taste, buy and eat, and stay the night. In Cochem the [Hieronimi](/en/locations/hieronimi) family has welcomed guests for more than 35 years in vaulted cellars by the river. In the Weingarten you sit in deckchairs by the water, looking up at the Reichsburg.

## Tip

Don't drive the whole Mosel in one day: the road follows every bend of the river. Choose a base such as Bernkastel, and take the bike or the boat to the villages nearby. All addresses are also in the [Mosel guide](/en/wine-travel/mosel).

title: Nederlandse wijngaarden bezoeken: van Zuid-Limburg tot Friesland
description: Wijngaarden waar je kunt proeven, van de Apostelhoeve in Maastricht tot De Frysling in Friesland: zo ontdek je Nederlandse wijn.
title_en: Visiting Dutch vineyards: from South Limburg to Friesland
description_en: Vineyards where you can taste, from the Apostelhoeve in Maastricht to De Frysling in Friesland: how to discover Dutch wine.
body_en:
The Netherlands now has hundreds of vineyards, and the wine gets better every year. South Limburg has the longest tradition, but there are vines in Zeeland, the Betuwe, the Achterhoek and even Friesland too. Many vineyards work with fungus-resistant grapes, such as Solaris, Johanniter and Souvignier Gris. These need little or no spraying. Below are the vineyards where you can taste.

## South Limburg

On the Louwberg above the Jeker valley lies [De Apostelhoeve](/en/locations/de-apostelhoeve), the oldest vineyard in the Netherlands, where wine has been made commercially since 1970. You can walk or cycle there from Maastricht. On the other side of the city is [Hoeve Nekum](/en/locations/wijngoed-hoeve-nekum), a courtyard farm from around 1600, with vines since 1988.

In Voerendaal, [Wijngoed Fromberg](/en/locations/wijngoed-fromberg) has made wine since 1994 on a south-facing limestone slope. In 1996 Fromberg released the first Dutch sparkling wine. You taste on a terrace with a view, and there is also a tour with sparkling wine and chocolate. [Domein Holset](/en/locations/domein-holset), near Vaals and the three-country point, makes only sparkling wine, in a farmhouse rebuilt with circular materials.

In Sint Geertruid, Marc and Eedsje Huynen started in 2016 with 325 vines in their back garden. Today [Wijndomein D'Hunes](/en/locations/wijndomein-dhunes) has seven hectares with eleven grape varieties. [Wijngoed Raar Saint Remi](/en/locations/wijngoed-raar-saint-remi) in Meerssen refers to the monks of Saint-Remi from Reims, who already had vineyards here in the Middle Ages. At [Sterreheim](/en/locations/sterreheim) in Schinnen, classic grape varieties grow around a 19th-century farmstead, and the alpacas provide the manure. In the white town of Thorn, in Central Limburg, winemaker Harry Vorselen talks about winemaking in the tasting room of [Wijngoed Thorn](/en/locations/wijngoed-thorn). Be sure to try the white wines there.

![De Apostelhoeve above the Jeker valley](/uploads/apostelhoeve.webp)

## Zeeland and the Betuwe

On Schouwen-Duiveland, [De Kleine Schorre](/en/locations/wijnhoeve-de-kleine-schorre) planted its first vines in 2001, with help from a Luxembourg wine house. Pinot Gris, Pinot Blanc, Rivaner and Auxerrois grow here, white wines that go well with Zeeland fish and shellfish. With some 63,000 vines it is one of the largest vineyards in the Netherlands. In Erichem, near Buren, the [Betuws Wijndomein](/en/locations/betuws-wijndomein) has seven hectares of fungus-resistant varieties only. You can walk and taste there all year round.

![De Kleine Schorre on Schouwen-Duiveland](/uploads/wijnhoeve-de-kleine-schorre.webp)

## The east and the north

Just outside Winterswijk lies [Wijngaard Hesselink](/en/locations/wijngaard-hesselink), on the cycle network. The tasting gives you five wines with bread and cheese. In Hilversum, [Wijngaard Zonnestraal](/en/locations/wijngaard-zonnestraal) has made wine since 2016, with a pizza and wine evening on the first Friday of each month. In Twijzel, in Friesland, is [De Frysling](/en/locations/wijngaard-de-frysling), one of the northernmost vineyards in the Netherlands. They make, among other things, the sparkling Brûswyn.

## In the city

[Chateau Amsterdam](/en/locations/chateau-amsterdam) in Amsterdam-Noord has no vineyard. It is an urban winery that turns grapes from Germany, France and Spain, among other places, into wine on the IJ. There is a tasting room and a restaurant.

## Tip

Many Dutch vineyards are only open at weekends or by appointment, and some only from spring to autumn. Check the website first. The sparkling wines are often the best place to start. All addresses are also on the [wine map](/en/wine-map).

title: Barolo en Barbaresco bezoeken: wijnhuizen, wijnbars en restaurants in de Langhe
description: Welke wijnhuizen je in Barolo en Barbaresco kunt bezoeken, waar je een glas nebbiolo drinkt en waar je eet: zo plan je een wijnreis door de Langhe.
title_en: Visiting Barolo and Barbaresco: wineries, wine bars and restaurants in the Langhe
description_en: Which wineries you can visit in Barolo and Barbaresco, where to drink a glass of Nebbiolo and where to eat: how to plan a wine trip through the Langhe.
body_en:
The Langhe, the hills around Alba, are home to Italy's two best-known wines: Barolo and Barbaresco, both from the Nebbiolo grape. The villages are a few kilometres apart, and each has a winery, an enoteca and a trattoria. Below, village by village, where to go.

## The region in brief

Barolo comes from eleven municipalities south-west of Alba, Barbaresco from three to the east. Barolo is usually more powerful, with more tannin, and needs longer ageing. Barbaresco is often a little more elegant. Within Barolo the villages differ too: wine from La Morra is often softer and more perfumed, from Serralunga d'Alba and Monforte firmer. Besides Nebbiolo, Barbera, Dolcetto and the white Arneis grow here. In Novello they are making the white Nascetta again.

## Barolo and La Morra

In the village of Barolo is [Cantina Bartolo Mascarello](/en/locations/cantina-bartolo-mascarello), the house of the region's best-known traditionalist, now run by his daughter Maria Teresa. On the Via Roma, [Vinoland](/en/locations/vinoland) has wines from large and small producers, including older vintages of twenty to thirty years. In the middle of the Cannubi cru lies [Locanda in Cannubi](/en/locations/locanda-in-cannubi), with around 825 wines and three pages of Barolo Cannubi from different producers. That way you taste the vineyard you are looking at.

In La Morra, [Osteria Veglio](/en/locations/osteria-veglio) has a terrace looking out over Barolo. The owner sometimes brings older vintages up from the cellar for the same price. [Mauro Molino](/en/locations/azienda-agricola-mauro-molino) in Annunziata makes Barolo in a modern style, a good introduction. [Dosio](/en/locations/dosio-vigneti) lies at 500 metres, the highest point in Barolo. For fine dining, go to [Belsit](/en/locations/belsit), with a cellar in the style of Gaudí. For traditional food, go to [L'Osteria del Vignaiolo](/en/locations/losteria-del-vignaiolo).

![Locanda in Cannubi among the vineyards](/uploads/locanda-in-cannubi.webp)

## Monforte, Castiglione Falletto and Serralunga

In Monforte d'Alba, at [Barolo Bar](/en/locations/barolo-bar) on the market square, you drink a glass with antipasti, with a roof terrace opposite. In Castiglione Falletto, [Casa Sobrero](/en/locations/casa-sobrero) has a tasting room and a terrace with views from La Morra to Serralunga. [Le Torri](/en/locations/le-torri) on the village square looks out over the vineyards.

In Serralunga d'Alba, [Palladino](/en/locations/azienda-vinicola-palladino) makes Barolo from its own vineyards in crus such as Vigna Rionda and Cerretta. After 35 years at Vietti, Elena Penna and Luca Currado started a new estate there: [Penna-Currado](/en/locations/penna-currado). Below the castle, [Vinoteca Centro Storico](/en/locations/vinoteca-centro-storico) has three antipasti, three primi and three secondi every day. On the Fontanafredda estate, Ugo Alciati cooks at [Guido](/en/locations/guido-ristorante), with a Michelin star and his mother's agnolotti del plin.

## Novello and Verduno

Novello is the quietest Barolo village. At [Langotto](/en/locations/langotto-ristorante), sommelier Elisa Andreotti helps you choose. Ask for a glass of Nascetta and a Barolo from the Ravera cru. At [Cogli l'Attimo](/en/locations/cogli-lattimo) you taste at picnic tables under big trees, without a cellar or reception. In Verduno, the least-known Barolo village, the brothers of [Fratelli Alessandria](/en/locations/fratelli-alessandria) welcome you in an old stone winery.

## Barbaresco, Neive and Treiso

In Barbaresco, [Produttori del Barbaresco](/en/locations/produttori-del-barbaresco) is a cooperative of 53 growers, founded in 1894. [Marchesi di Grésy](/en/locations/marchesi-di-grésy) has owned the Martinenga vineyard since 1797. [Ronchi](/en/locations/azienda-agricola-ronchi) is a small family estate with seven hectares. You eat at [Antica Torre](/en/locations/antica-torre), a family restaurant with rabbit, truffle and pasta.

In Neive, [Al nido della Cinciallegra](/en/locations/al-nido-della-cinciallegra) on the village square is the oldest enoteca in the village, full of local wines. In Treiso, [Ca' del Baio](/en/locations/ca-del-baio) lies in a natural amphitheatre of vineyards, and [Villa Garassino](/en/locations/villa-garassino) is an agriturismo looking out over Barbaresco.

![Produttori del Barbaresco](/uploads/produttori-del-barbaresco.webp)

## Alba and the surroundings

In Alba, [Vincafè](/en/locations/vincafè) on the Via Vittorio Emanuele pours more than sixty Piedmontese wines. [La Piola](/en/locations/la-piola) on the Piazza Risorgimento is the Ceretto family's simple restaurant, opposite the cathedral. On the Piazza Michele Ferrero the Sarotto family has a wine bar: [Roberto Sarotto](/en/locations/roberto-sarotto). A little further away are [Poderi Luigi Einaudi](/en/locations/poderi-luigi-einaudi-azienda-agricola) in Dogliani, where you can also stay, [Trattoria del Peso](/en/locations/trattoria-del-peso) in Belvedere Langhe, where you eat whatever is cooking that day, and [Le Piemontesine](/en/locations/le-piemontesine) in the Alta Langa.

## Tip

Come in autumn for the white truffle of Alba, or in spring when it is quieter. At most wineries you need to book ahead. All addresses are also in the [Piedmont guide](/en/wine-travel/piedmont).

title: Wijn in Antwerpen: wijnbars en wijnrestaurants per wijk
description: Van natuurwijn op het Zuid tot 800 wijnen in een zeemanskerk op het Eilandje: de wijnbars, wijnwinkels en wijnrestaurants van Antwerpen, per wijk.
title_en: Wine in Antwerp: wine bars and wine restaurants by neighbourhood
description_en: From natural wine in het Zuid to 800 wines in a seamen's church on the Eilandje: the wine bars, wine shops and wine restaurants of Antwerp, by neighbourhood.
body_en:
Antwerp is easy to explore on foot, and its wine addresses are in three areas: the old town around the Meir, het Zuid and the Eilandje by the docks. Het Zuid has the natural wine bars, the Eilandje the restaurants with big wine lists. Below, by neighbourhood, where to go.

## The old town

On the Geefsstraat, close to the Meir, [Het Archief](/en/locations/het-archief) is in the former Provincial Archive from 1851. There are always more than 25 wines open by the glass, and some of them change every day. On the Hopland, [Luddites](/en/locations/luddites-books-wine) is a bookshop with a wine bar upstairs, in a townhouse from 1902. There is no wifi, and if you buy a book you get a glass of wine at half price.

On the Schermersstraat, [Amber Bottle Shop](/en/locations/amber-bottle-shop) sells more than 400 natural wines, partly imported by the owners, and you can also have a glass at the bar. At [Belgian Wines](/en/locations/belgian-wines) on the Oudevaartplaats there is only Belgian wine on the list: sparkling, white, rosé and red, with local cheese and charcuterie. If you want to eat, go to [Invincible](/en/locations/invincible) on the Haarstraat, where cook and sommelier Kenny Burssens serves modern French food at a long counter with plenty of wine by the glass.

![Het Archief on the Geefsstraat](/uploads/het-archief.webp)

## Het Zuid

Het Zuid has two wine bars for anyone who wants to taste something new. [Spiridon](/en/locations/spiridon) on the Kronenburgstraat pours mainly natural wine, with small dishes such as veal tongue with salsa verde. An old butcher's fridge serves as the wine cellar. At [Ta-nnin](/en/locations/ta-nnin) on the Volkstraat around 25 wines are open by the glass, with classic regions next to wines from Central and Eastern Europe. The small dishes have Japanese, Korean and Italian influences.

![Spiridon in het Zuid](/uploads/spiridon.webp)

## The Eilandje

On the Eilandje, the old dock area, you eat with a big wine list. [Marcel](/en/locations/restaurant-marcel) is in a former seamen's church next to the MAS and has around 800 wines, more than 40 of them by the glass. In an old warehouse on the Oudeleeuwenrui, [Pazzo](/en/locations/pazzo) has a restaurant with hundreds of wines, and a wine bar upstairs with more than 170, most of them by the glass. [Bistrot L'îlot](/en/locations/bistrot-lilot) on the Kribbestraat is smaller: a thirty-seat bistro with a menu that follows the market and mostly French wine at friendly prices.

On the top floor of the MAS is [Zilte](/en/locations/zilte), with three Michelin stars and views over the docks. Sommelier Aaron Moeraert pours several wines by the glass with each dish, so you can choose yourself.

## Outside the centre

In the De Koninck city brewery, [The Butcher's Son](/en/locations/the-butchers-son) has a Michelin star. Red meat is the focus, with a list of around 400 wines, mostly from France, Italy and Spain. In Edegem, a fifteen-minute drive away, [Stable](/en/locations/stable) is in the old stables of an 18th-century castle, with a good Belgian selection on the wine list.

## Tip

Combine the wine bars of het Zuid in one evening: Spiridon and Ta-nnin are a few minutes' walk apart. All addresses are also in the [Antwerp guide](/en/wine-tips/antwerp).

title: Wijn in Málaga en Marbella: wijnbars, bodega's en wijnhuizen
description: Van zoete moscatel uit het vat in de oudste wijnbar van Málaga tot droge wijn van steile hellingen in de Axarquía: zo drink je wijn in Málaga en Marbella.
title_en: Wine in Málaga and Marbella: wine bars, bodegas and wineries
description_en: From sweet Moscatel from the barrel in Málaga's oldest wine bar to dry wine from steep slopes in the Axarquía: how to drink wine in Málaga and Marbella.
body_en:
Málaga is best known for sweet wine, made from Moscatel and Pedro Ximénez. You still drink it from the barrel in the old bodegas of the centre. But in the city's wine bars and in the mountains around it you will also find dry wine from small producers. Below are the addresses in Málaga, the wineries nearby and the wine bars in Marbella.

## The classics in the centre

[Antigua Casa de Guardia](/en/locations/antigua-casa-de-guardia) on the Alameda Principal is the oldest wine bar in Málaga, open since 1840. Along the back wall lie 24 oak barrels, and the barmen pour the wine straight into small glasses. Your bill is chalked on the bar. Try the Pajarete, a semi-sweet wine typical of Málaga, or the dry Seco Añejo. A glass rarely costs more than a few euros.

[El Pimpi](/en/locations/el-pimpi), in an 18th-century mansion opposite the Roman theatre, is a little touristy, but always lively. The list is built around wines from Málaga and the Sierras de Málaga, from producers such as Doña Felisa and Jorge Ordóñez. Order a vino dulce. At [La Tranca](/en/locations/la-tranca) on the Calle Carretería you drink the house vermouth, among classic tapas and a loud crowd.

![Antigua Casa de Guardia on the Alameda Principal](/uploads/antigua.webp)

## Wine bars for new discoveries

[Los Patios de Beatas](/en/locations/los-patios-de-beatas), close to the Picasso Museum, has more than 600 wines, over 50 of them by the glass, in two restored buildings with patios. At [Vertical](/en/locations/vertical) you don't just order a glass: sommelier Julio Barluenga first asks what you like and then lets you taste wines from small producers. Book, because it is small.

[Descorche](/en/locations/descorche) on the Calle Álamos has many wines from Málaga and natural wine, and the small dishes are matched to the wine. Come here to taste something other than the well-known Rioja and Ribera del Duero. At [Vinoteca Bouquet](/en/locations/vinoteca-bouquet) on the Alameda you get an explanation with every wine from the two Cuban brothers who run it. [Anyway Winebar](/en/locations/anyway-winebar) by the harbour pours mainly Spanish wine, with a lot by the glass, from sherry to red. If you want to eat, go to [Araboka](/en/locations/araboka) near the cathedral: the list has many wines from the province of Málaga, and with the menu you get a sweet Málaga wine with dessert.

For a bottle to take away, go to [Crespillo Innova](/en/locations/crespillo-innova), a wine shop and butcher in one. Top Spanish wines cost a good deal less here than in the Netherlands.

![The patio of Los Patios de Beatas](/uploads/beatas.webp)

## Wineries around Málaga

[Bodegas Quitapenas](/en/locations/bodegas-quitapenas) in Churriana, founded in 1880 and now run by the fifth generation, is close to the airport. You taste three or four wines there, with cheese or Ibérico ham if you like. In the Axarquía, east of Málaga, the vineyards lie on steep slopes. [Bodegas Bentomiz](/en/locations/bodegas-bentomiz) in Sayalonga was founded by a Dutch couple and lies at 500 to 800 metres, looking out to sea. [Fabio Coullet](/en/locations/bodega-fabio-coullet) in Almáchar makes dry wines from old local grapes, such as the almost forgotten Romé. That is unusual in a region known mainly for sweet wine. [Bodegas Jorge Ordóñez](/en/locations/bodega-ordonez) in Vélez-Málaga, which specialises in Moscatel, also receives visitors by appointment.

In the mountains near Ronda, [Bodega Doña Felisa](/en/locations/bodega-doña-felisa) lies at around 900 metres, close to the Roman ruins of Acinipo. The tour takes an hour and a half, with a tasting and snacks. Near Manilva, on the coast, [Nilva](/en/locations/nilva-enoturismo) is saving the old Moscatel vines; the tasting takes place in a vineyard with views of Gibraltar and the African coast.

## Marbella

In Nueva Andalucía, sommelier Emilio Campos runs [Adivino](/en/locations/adivino): wine bar, wine shop and gallery in one space, with guided tastings, blind ones too. [G-Wine](/en/locations/g-wine-bar-and-grill) in San Pedro pours more than 25 wines by the glass, seven days a week. At [Lobito de Mar](/en/locations/lobito-de-mar) you eat fish and bluefin tuna, in seventeen preparations, with a serious wine list. And [Cascada](/en/locations/cascada), in the hills of the Sierra Blanca, has a five-course menu with a €30 wine pairing.

## Tip

In Málaga, taste the wines of the region itself, sweet and dry. Many restaurants mostly pour well-known wines from Rioja and Ribera del Duero, while the wines from the province itself are far more interesting. All addresses are also in the [Málaga & Marbella guide](/en/wine-travel/malaga).

title: Wijnbars in Rotterdam: waar drink je wat, per buurt
description: Van zelf tappen in Blijdorp tot natuurwijn op Katendrecht: de wijnbars, wijnwinkels en wijnrestaurants van Rotterdam, per buurt.
title_en: Wine bars in Rotterdam: where to drink what, by neighbourhood
description_en: From pouring your own in Blijdorp to natural wine on Katendrecht: the wine bars, wine shops and wine restaurants of Rotterdam, by neighbourhood.
body_en:
Rotterdam has plenty of wine bars, spread across the city. In the centre you find the classics with big lists, on Katendrecht and in the Oude Noorden mostly natural wine. Below, by neighbourhood, where to go.

## City centre

[Wijnbar Het Eigendom](/en/locations/wijnbar-het-eigendom) opened in 2011 as the first wine bar on the Witte de Withstraat, in a building from the 1940s. There are 135 wines on the list, 35 of them by the glass, and more than twenty small dishes. On the Hoogstraat, [Café Verward](/en/locations/café-verward) pours plenty of natural wine without a fixed list: Ward asks what you like and pours accordingly. On the Goudsesingel are [Bar Bocht](/en/locations/bar-bocht), with natural wine and Champagne from small producers, and [Wijnkoperij Platenburg](/en/locations/wijnkoperij-platenburg), a wine shop almost 130 years old with more than 1,000 wines. Next to the shop, in the wine bar Proef, you can drink special wines by the glass every day.

Close to Rotterdam Centraal, at [L'Ouest](/en/locations/louest) you choose a wine flight: three wines with snacks and an explanation, often from lesser-known regions. [Vineum](/en/locations/vineum) on the Eendrachtsweg has more than 1,750 wines on its list. Thanks to the Coravin you can taste expensive wines by the glass too, downstairs in the wine bar or upstairs in the restaurant. On the Veerhaven, [Louise Petit](/en/locations/louise-petit-restaurant) has a French bistro with a separate Bar à Vins, where you drink a glass of Loire or Champagne with a cheese board.

![Wijnbar Het Eigendom on the Witte de Withstraat](/uploads/eigendom.webp)

## Katendrecht and the Kop van Zuid

On Katendrecht, [NOTK](/en/locations/notk) on the Delistraat is restaurant, wine bar and wine shop at once. A few doors down, [De Matroos en het Meisje](/en/locations/de-matroos-en-het-meisje) has a small list of mostly organic and natural wine, plenty of Champagne and Burgundy, and half glasses at all times. Sommelier Taco de Vos also runs [Eetcafé 't Meisje](/en/locations/eetcafé-t-meisje) on the Brede Hilledijk, where you can walk in without booking for a glass and a plate of comfort food. Under the Entrepot building is [Tres](/en/locations/tres), with a Michelin star and sixteen seats at the counter.

![NOTK on Katendrecht](/uploads/notk.jpg)

## The Oude Noorden, Blijdorp and Kralingen

On the Proveniersstraat two addresses sit side by side. [Le Nord](/en/locations/le-nord) is a wine shop downstairs and a tasting room upstairs, with an open tasting every month. At [Café Kiem](/en/locations/café-kiem) you drink natural wine with local, seasonal food. Around the corner, at [Klaargemaakt](/en/locations/klaargemaakt) on the Schiekade, the list also has plenty of natural wine, next to home-made fermented drinks.

At [Walsjérôt](/en/locations/wijnbar-walsjérôt) in Blijdorp you load a card and pour your own: a sip, a half or a full glass, from more than 70 wines. In Kralingen, [Juni](/en/locations/juni-rotterdam) treats wine and cheese as equal partners. You can't book, so you just walk in. [LUX](/en/locations/lux) on the 's-Gravendijkwal pours natural wine only, with a four-course menu.

## Delfshaven

In historic Delfshaven, Fred and Monique Zywiecki have run ['t Ouwe Bruggetje](/en/locations/t-ouwe-bruggetje) since 1989, with a terrace on the water. Nearly all the wines come from their own imports, and whatever you drink with dinner you can buy afterwards in the wine shop next door.

## Tip

Many of Rotterdam's natural wine bars are small, and some don't take bookings. Come early. All addresses are also in the [Rotterdam guide](/en/wine-tips/rotterdam).

title: Wijn in 't Gooi: wijnbars en wijnwinkels in Bussum, Laren en Blaricum
description: Van een Italiaanse wijnbar in Baarn tot een wijnwinkel in een boerderij in Laren: de wijnadressen van 't Gooi, per plaats.
title_en: Wine in Het Gooi: wine bars and wine shops in Bussum, Laren and Blaricum
description_en: From an Italian wine bar in Baarn to a wine shop in a Laren farmhouse: the wine addresses of Het Gooi, town by town.
body_en:
Het Gooi is small, but it has plenty of good wine addresses. Bussum and Laren each have a few wine shops with a large range. In Blaricum and Baarn there are wine bars where you can taste a lot by the glass. Below, town by town, where to go.

## Bussum

In the centre of Bussum, on the Kerkstraat, is [The Winebar](/en/locations/the-winebar), from the same owner as A-Fusion, so the food is good too. The wine list is simple, but ask for the notebook: it holds a few top wines. Around the corner, on the Kapelstraat, [de Buren](/en/locations/de-buren) pours original wines, such as a Nebbiolo from South Africa, next to familiar names. They charge a fixed mark-up per bottle, which keeps a good bottle affordable.

For a bottle to take home, go to the [Bussumsche Wijnkooperij](/en/locations/bussumsche-wijnkooperij) on the Spiegelstraat. Besides a large range of wine they have older vintages and top wines. Ask for Howard for advice on wine with food. [Wijnhandel Eduard Mol](/en/locations/wijnhandel-eduard-mol) on the Huizerweg has long been a fixture in Bussum. The shop is a little cluttered, but there is always something open to taste.

![De Bussumsche Wijnkooperij on the Spiegelstraat](/uploads/bow.webp)

## Laren and Blaricum

[De Larense Wijnkoperij](/en/locations/de-larense-wijnkoperij) is in a listed farmhouse on the Torenlaan, with more than 600 wines, many of them imported by the owners. At [Visatelier](/en/locations/visatelier-laren) in Laren a fishmonger, a restaurant and a wine bar share one roof. In the wine bar you drink sparkling or white wine, without having to eat.

In Blaricum, [Ottovino](/en/locations/ottovino) on the Dorpsstraat pours more than thirty wines by the glass. Owner Otto collects the wines himself from the estates, often small producers, and you can take your favourite bottle straight home. [Wexxs](/en/locations/wexxs) is also in a farmhouse, on the Torenlaan in Blaricum. At the end of the day there is often something open to taste. If you want to eat, there is [Bistrôt Chapeau](/en/locations/bistrôt-chapeau) on the Huizerweg for French bistro dishes, or [Rust Wat](/en/locations/rust-wat-by-sidney-schutte) on the Schapendrift for a French brasserie with fish and aged meat.

![De Larense Wijnkoperij in a farmhouse on the Torenlaan](/uploads/dlw.jpg)

## Baarn, Hilversum and Huizen

[Vineria Nebbiolo](/en/locations/vineria-nebbiolo) in Baarn has 450 Italian wines, from Trentino-Alto Adige to Sicily, with an Italian menu that changes every week. Per bottle you pay a fixed €15 on top of the shop price. In Hilversum, [Gastrovino Mijn Hemel](/en/locations/gastrovino-mijn-hemel) is a wine shop with a wine café: you taste by the glass first and take a bottle home afterwards. On the edge of Hilversum lies [Wijngaard Zonnestraal](/en/locations/wijngaard-zonnestraal), the only vineyard in Het Gooi, with its first harvest in 2016. There are regular events, such as a pizza and wine evening on the first Friday of each month. In Huizen, [Siersma Wijnadvies](/en/locations/siersma-wijnadvies) sells, among other things, its own Skaap wines from South Africa.

![Vineria Nebbiolo in Baarn](/uploads/nebbiolo.webp)

## Around Het Gooi

By the lock in Muiden is [Wijnbar Vijf](/en/locations/wijnbar-vijf), with wines from small estates and a large menu of dishes to share. In Weesp, [Somm](/en/locations/somm-bistro-à-vin) has more than 250 wines, from affordable to exclusive. In Vreeland and Loenen aan de Vecht there are two restaurants with a Michelin star: [De Nederlanden](/en/locations/de-nederlanden), with a broad wine list, and ['t Amsterdammertje](/en/locations/t-amsterdammertje), with organic wines only.

## Tip

Many wine shops in Het Gooi have something open to taste at the end of the week. Combine a visit with a drink in one of the wine bars. All addresses are also in the [Het Gooi guide](/en/wine-tips/het-gooi).

title: Wijnbars en wijnwinkels in Utrecht: waar drink je wat
description: Van natuurwijn in de Nachtegaalstraat tot vijftig wijnen per glas bij de Dom: de wijnbars, wijnwinkels en wijnrestaurants van Utrecht.
title_en: Wine bars and wine shops in Utrecht: where to drink what
description_en: From natural wine on the Nachtegaalstraat to fifty wines by the glass by the Dom: the wine bars, wine shops and wine restaurants of Utrecht.
body_en:
In Utrecht most wine bars are within walking distance of each other, around the Dom, the Neude and the Oudegracht. Many of them pour natural wine, and in Utrecht-Oost there are two wine shops that specialise in it. Below are the addresses, by type.

## Wine bars around the Neude and the Dom

[VinVin](/en/locations/wijnbar-vinvin) on the Predikherenstraat, open since 2016, has no printed wine list: the staff help you choose from some thirty wines by French, Italian and Spanish producers who intervene as little as possible. On the Neude, [Wijncafé Lefebvre](/en/locations/wijncafé-lefebvre) pours 27 wines by the glass in three price ranges, and you can taste a few first. On the Lange Jansstraat is [Wijnbar Kurk](/en/locations/wijnbar-kurk), a small wine bar with old wooden cabinets. The team takes you through the list glass by glass. On Fridays and Saturdays it is walk-in only.

Between the Domplein and the Oudegracht, [Talud9](/en/locations/talud9) has more than 50 wines by the glass, mostly European and partly natural. On 't Wed, close to the Dom, [Bar Bet](/en/locations/bar-bet) has around 250 bottles and 30 wines by the glass, with classics and natural wine side by side and a terrace by the water.

![Talud9 on the Donkere Gaard](/uploads/talud9.webp)

## On the canals

On the Oudegracht, [VINO](/en/locations/wijnbar-vino) is in the Winkel van Sinkel, the first department store in the Netherlands. There are more than 140 wines on the list, and you can order a high wine with five wines and five dishes. [Jacob's](/en/locations/jacobs-wine-gastrobar-union-house) in Union House looks out on the old Tivoli and has a few original wines next to familiar names. On the Nieuwegracht, [Proeflokaal de Lindebar](/en/locations/proeflokaal-de-lindebar) has special wines, but also whisky, port and jenever. A few times a month you can walk in for a tasting without booking.

## Eating with a good glass

At [Café-Restaurant Terroir](/en/locations/café-restaurant-terroir) in the Museumkwartier you choose your wine first and then your dish. There are around 500 wines on the list, with a fixed margin per bottle and a lot of German wine, Burgundy and natural wine. [Rosie](/en/locations/rosie) on the Lucasbolwerk is half restaurant, half bar, with plenty of natural wine and oysters at the bar. In the Polman's Huis, [Hemel & Aarde](/en/locations/hemel-aarde) has a restaurant and a wine bar, with wines that change with the seasons. [Bistro Madeleine](/en/locations/bistro-madeleine) on 't Wed is a French bistro with a long bar, also good for a glass and a bite. At [San Siro](/en/locations/san-siro) on the Oudkerkhof the list is mostly Italian, and nearly everything is available by the glass.

Just outside the centre are [Restaurant Badhuis](/en/locations/restaurant-badhuis), in a bathhouse from 1927 with dishes from the grill over an open fire, and [De Watertoren](/en/locations/restaurant-de-watertoren) in Rotsoord, with views over the city. At [Vondels Chefs Bar](/en/locations/vondels-chefs-bar) in the Dichterswijk there is deliberately no set wine pairing: the staff help you discover something yourself.

![Café-Restaurant Terroir in the Museumkwartier](/uploads/terroirutrechtwebp.webp)

## Wine shops

On the Nachtegaalstraat in Utrecht-Oost, two wine shops are a few doors apart. [Vleck](/en/locations/vleck-wijnen) sells natural wine from small winemakers. There are also many clear, classic-tasting bottles, and on Fridays there is often a small tasting. At [Chatobi](/en/locations/chatobi) you only find wines from small estates the owner has visited and tasted in person.

In the city centre, [De Vinotheek](/en/locations/de-vinotheek) on the Hardebollenstraat has around eighty organic and natural wines, from the same owner as VinVin. [Utregs Wijnhuis](/en/locations/utregs-wijnhuis) is behind the Dom and has everything from an everyday bottle to exclusive wine. [Welkom aan Tafel](/en/locations/welkom-aan-tafel) on the Lange Smeestraat is an importer working with more than 50 European estates, with a tasting cellar under the shop.

## Tip

Many wine bars in the centre are small, and at weekends you sometimes cannot book. Come early or try a few. All addresses are also in the [Utrecht guide](/en/wine-tips/utrecht).

title: De wijnbars van Amsterdam: waar drink je wat, per wijk
description: Van naturel in De Pijp tot Duitse riesling aan de Singel: de wijnbars van Amsterdam per wijk, met wat ze bijzonder maakt.
title_en: The wine bars of Amsterdam: where to drink what, by neighbourhood
description_en: From natural wine in De Pijp to German Riesling on the Singel: Amsterdam's wine bars by neighbourhood, and what makes each one special.
body_en:
Amsterdam now has dozens of wine bars, and every neighbourhood has its own character. In De Pijp it is mostly natural wine, around the canals you find the wine bars with big cellars, and in Oost and Noord you can combine a glass with a bottle to take home. Below are the wine bars we recommend, by area.

## De Pijp: natural wine and classics

In 2015 [GlouGlou](/en/locations/glouglou-1) opened in De Pijp, the first natural wine bar in the Netherlands. The list is natural wine only, and you sit on a small terrace among the flowers. Around the corner, on the Ceintuurbaan, is [Wijnbar Paulus](/en/locations/wijnbar-paulus), a fixture for more than ten years: a retro living room with eight to ten white and red wines by the glass, European only, with finds from Greece, Israel and Lebanon. On the Lutmastraat is [Wijnbar Paskamer](/en/locations/wijnbar-paskamer), linked to the Amsterdam Wine Academy; from four people you can book a tasting.

![Wijnbar Paulus in De Pijp](/uploads/paulus.webp)

## Around the Utrechtsestraat and the Frederiksplein

[Bar Babar](/en/locations/bar-babar) on the Utrechtsestraat feels like a small Parisian bistro: natural wines, candlelight and almost everything by the glass. The owners work with Amsterdam suppliers, from Mater's bread to the wines of Pieksman and Vleck. A few hundred metres away, on the Frederiksplein, [Oocker](/en/locations/oocker) mixes original wines with well-known favourites, plenty of them by the glass too.

![Bar Babar on the Utrechtsestraat](/uploads/babar.webp)

## The canals and the centre: big cellars

On the Prinsengracht, in the basement of [Sinck](/en/locations/sinck), is a wine bar with around 400 wines, mostly French, for every budget; sommelier Sabas Joosten previously worked at De Librije. [Weinlokal Stern](/en/locations/weinlokal-stern) on the Singel is as German as it gets: from Mosel Riesling to Spätburgunder from Baden, with schnitzel and spätzle. [Bar du Champagne](/en/locations/bar-du-champagne) on the Rokin pours only Champagne, from a cellar of more than 450 labels, with oysters and seafood. On the Lijnbaansgracht, [Wijnbar Shiraz](/en/locations/wijnbar-shiraz) has a broad list with plenty by the glass, even a 40-year-old tawny port. And on the Zeedijk, [Vermeers Wijnkamer](/en/locations/vermeers-wijnkamer) pours two wines with every bite: one under ten euros and one pricier.

![The basement wine bar at Sinck](/uploads/sinck.webp)

## Oud-West: neighbourhood bars with character

In Oud-West, Frenchman Paco runs [Bar François](/en/locations/bar-françois) on his own, from the kitchen to the wine list, with southern French dishes that change every week. On the Wilhelminastraat, [Barrica](/en/locations/barrica) combines Spanish and international wines with tapas, on one of the nicest terraces in the area.

![Bar François in Oud-West](/uploads/francois.jpg)

## Oost and Noord: wine bar and wine shop in one

[Bottleshop](/en/locations/bottleshop) on the Wibautstraat goes all in on natural wine, alongside sake, cider and Champagne. At [Clos](/en/locations/clos) on the Beukenplein you can choose from plenty of affordable wines by the glass and a high wine of three to five courses. Cross the IJ and in Noord you will find [Wijnbar Vindict](/en/locations/wijnbar-vindict): more than 50 wines by the glass and over 800 by the bottle, which you can also take home straight away.

![Bottleshop on the Wibautstraat](/uploads/bottleshop.webp)

## Tip

Many of these wine bars are small and fill up quickly in the evening. Book if you can, or come early in the evening. You will also find all the addresses on the [wine map](/en/wine-map) and in the [Amsterdam guide](/en/wine-tips/amsterdam).

title: Wijnbars in Parijs: van natuurwijn in Belleville tot grote wijnwinkels
description: Natuurwijnbars, staande wijnbars bij het Odéon en wijnwinkels met duizenden flessen: waar je in Parijs een goed glas drinkt.
title_en: Wine bars in Paris: from natural wine in Belleville to big wine shops
description_en: Natural wine bars, standing wine bars by the Odéon and wine shops with thousands of bottles: where to drink a good glass in Paris.
body_en:
Paris is one of the best cities in the world to drink wine, and since the 2000s also the city of natural wine. Almost every neighbourhood has a small bar à vins where you drink by the glass with a board of cheese and charcuterie. Below are the addresses we recommend, from natural wine bars to the big wine shops.

## Natural wine

[Garde Robe](/en/locations/garde-robe) on the Rue de l'Arbre Sec, close to the Louvre, has been one of the first natural wine bars in Paris since 2006. It is small, with many regulars. In Belleville, Julien Maillet turned an old betting shop into [Liquiderie](/en/locations/liquiderie-bar): more than 400 natural wines and 200 beers, with a whole wall of taps and low prices. At [Septime](/en/locations/septime) on the Rue de Charonne the list has plenty of biodynamic and natural wine. You need to book the restaurant well ahead, but you can also go to Septime La Cave, the wine bar around the corner.

![Garde Robe near the Louvre](/uploads/garde-robe.webp)

## Bars à vins in the neighbourhoods

In the Haut-Marais, [Le Barav](/en/locations/le-barav) has been a neighbourhood spot for more than fifteen years. There are 250 wines, and you can drink a bottle from the shop next door at the bar for a small corkage fee. At the foot of the Sacré-Cœur, [Les Piqueurs](/en/locations/les-piqueurs) chooses one winemaker per French appellation, usually organic or biodynamic, with a board of cheese and charcuterie. In the 9th arrondissement, [Duvin](/en/locations/duvin) has a broad, fairly priced list with winemakers such as Jean Foillard and Emmanuel Reynaud, and French bistro classics. [La Cave Pigalle](/en/locations/la-cave-pigalle) is the wine shop of 228 Litres, with more than 2,000 wines, plenty of grower Champagne and natural wine.

By the Odéon, three [Avant Comptoirs](/en/locations/lavant-comptoir-de-la-terre-et-mer) sit side by side: Terre, Mer and Marché. There are no tables and you can't book. You stand at the bar with a glass and small bites, such as oysters at Mer. [Willi's Wine Bar](/en/locations/le-willis-wine-bar) by the Palais-Royal is all about French wine, especially from the Rhône, with a bistro attached.

![The Avant Comptoirs by the Odéon](/uploads/avant-comptoir.webp)

## Wine shops

Close to the Palais-Royal, [Legrand Filles et Fils](/en/locations/legrand-filles-et-fils) has plenty of Burgundy, Rhône and Loire, with a separate room for Bordeaux. On Fridays and Saturdays there are often free tastings. At [Caves Augé](/en/locations/caves-augé) on the Boulevard Haussmann there are 3,000 to 4,000 wines. Once a month, winemakers pour their own wine at a free tasting on the pavement. [Lavinia](/en/locations/lavinia) on the Avenue Victor Hugo is the largest wine shop in Paris, with more than 6,500 wines. From the wine dispensers on the ground floor you taste small sips, from house wine to grand cru.

## Tip

Many small wine bars in Paris don't take bookings. Come early in the evening, around six. Combine the wine shops with a bar in the same area: Legrand and Willi's are a few minutes' walk apart, as are La Cave Pigalle and Duvin. All addresses are also in the [Paris guide](/en/wine-tips/paris).
